notes:
Summary: High-potential logistics customer evaluating Redwood Dedicated/Private for low-latency routing and high-burst chat support. POC ran for 3 weeks; functional fit OK but major scaling concerns.

Timeline snapshots:
- 2024-06-18: Intro call (AE Maya) - high-level product fit, want to replace slow internal API.
- 2024-07-10: Scoping workshop with ML infra + ops (SE Elliot) - workload: spikes during morning dispatch windows, peaks ~20k concurrent QPS across routing microservices.
- 2024-08-19: POC kickoff (fireflies ff-2024-08-19-9832) - 2 x Dedicated node baseline, synthetic burst generator.
- 2024-09-05: Mid-POC sync - observed tail latency and growing request queueing under 20% higher burst than baseline; Redwood team recommended larger burst pool + autoscale policy tweak.
- 2024-09-18: Security review submitted (drive doc) - asking for KMS integration + residency confirmation; legal reviewing.
- 2024-10-02: Emergency incident during simulated BlackFriday workload; queue depth exceeded SLO, fallbacks not exercised as planned (fireflies ff-2024-10-02-1145).
- 2024-10-15: Customer paused procurement while evaluating in-house rewrite and cloud-managed endpoints; internal Head of ML left company.
- 2024-11-20: Competitor (in-house) demo accepted by ops; budget freeze communicated by CFO pending exec review.

Technical notes:
- Root cause: current POC sizing under-provisioned for peak burst patterns; autoscaler reacts too slowly to sudden spikes; KV cache warmup latency amplified tail.
- Customer requested deterministic throughput SLOs and predictable burst capacity (reserved burst lanes) — asked for hard guarantees rather than probabilistic autoscaling.
- Suggested mitigations provided: pre-warmed burst pools, API-side backpressure, adaptive batching thresholds, and on-call runbook for cache warmup. Customer wants an expanded soak test (72h) with 3x burst multiplier before moving forward.

Commercial / org notes:
- AE impression: strong product interest but no clear champion after personnel changes. Procurement timeline slipped.
- Competitive pressure: internal rebuild looked cheaper on paper; GCP Vertex endpoints also evaluated for simpler procurement path.

Next steps / open items:
- Offer extended stress POC with dedicated pre-warmed burst nodes (cost estimate in drive).
- Ask legal to fast-track residency confirmation and signability of addendum for KMS.
- Re-engage exec sponsor (SVP Ops) to regain champion or identify alternate sponsor.
- If procurement remains frozen by 2024-12-15 mark as closed-lost and schedule periodic nurture cadence.

CRM style notes / snippets from calls:
- "Need hard guarantees for peak windows — can't have intermittent queueing" (VP Ops)
- "If we can prove steady tail latency under 200ms at peak, we can move to purchase" (Head of Engineering, now left)
- "We're leaning to build this ourselves unless Redwood can show deterministic burst lanes"

Reason for stall/loss: technical fit on burst throughput and queueing; operational appetite to build in-house coupled with Q4 budget freeze and no internal champion.
